Well, it's that time of year again — autumn, and I'm getting ready to sow wheat. I've got 16.9 mu total. About 14 mu goes into wheat-maize double cropping like always, and I keep about 3 mu in cotton on the side. My boy works in town now, so it's mainly me and my wife handling the day-to-day, though he comes back for harvest if he can get away.

**Wheat** — I'll sow around October 10th, maybe a day or two earlier if the soil is still warm. The extension agent says mid-October is ideal, but I've been doing this 30 years and I know my land. I'm using an improved variety — I saved some seed from last year but bought about half new bags from the seed shop for 4 yuan per mu. Can't trust saved seed forever, rust gets worse. For fertilizer, I'll put down roughly 100 jin of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 type — as basal before sowing. That's about 7.5 kg each of N, P, and K per mu right there. Then at jointing, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I'll topdress with urea, maybe another 10 kg N per mu. The extension guy says 15 kg N per mu total is enough, but I usually do a bit more — last year I did about 18 kg N and got 500 kg per mu. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad yield. Irrigation is 4 times: once before winter if it's dry, then green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Pumping costs money — about 5 yuan per mu each time — but you can't skip it, the well water is metered now. For chemicals, I'll spray herbicide once before planting, insecticide twice for aphids, and fungicide once for powdery mildew. I'll do rotary tillage to prepare the wheat bed. Labor is mostly family — me and my wife — but I might hire one day of help at harvest if we're short.

**Maize** — After wheat harvest in early June, the window is tight. Maybe 5–7 days, sometimes less if it rains. I'll plant mid-June, right into the wheat stubble with no-tillage or just a light pass. No time for proper tillage. I buy hybrid maize seed every year — never save it, doesn't work — costs about 8 yuan per mu. Fertilizer goes down with the seed: about 80 jin of compound per mu, then I'll topdress urea when the plants are knee-high. Total around 12 kg N per mu, plus some P and K from the compound. I'll irrigate twice: once at seedling stage if it's dry, and once at tasseling — that's the critical time, you miss that and you lose yield. Herbicide once, insecticide twice for corn borer. Yield should be around 550 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Cotton** — I plant mid-April on the 3 mu. It's a lot of work, all that spraying. I use an improved variety, seed costs about 15 yuan per mu. Basal fertilizer is compound, about 10 kg N per mu total with some P and K. I'll irrigate twice — flowering and boll stage — cotton doesn't like wet feet. The real cost is pesticide. Bollworm is terrible some years. I'll spray insecticide maybe 12 times through summer, plus herbicide once. That's why I only keep 3 mu of cotton — too much labor and chemical cost. But the lint price has been okay, so it pays. I do rotary tillage for cotton. Picking is the worst — me and my wife do most of it, but I usually hire 3 days of help.

Total input costs will be around 2,400 yuan this year. It's a lot, but last year was decent and I have some cash put aside. I'm not changing much — why fix what isn't broken? Though I did hear my neighbor down the road tried a new wheat variety and got maybe 50 kg more per mu. Hmm. Maybe next year.
